# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC address | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F |
| Logged-in domain user | ccollier (domain: wiresharkworkshop.online, DC = 172.16.1.4 / WIRESHARK-WS-DC) |

Hostname and MAC confirmed via NBNS Name Service traffic (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>` from 172.16.1.66) and Ethernet source address on all frames from that IP. The logged-on user was confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString fields (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`) exchanged with the domain controller.

## 2. Malware Family
**STRRAT** (Java-based RAT/credential-stealer, distributed as a `.jar` payload, no dependency on OS platform).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The C2 beacon traffic contains the malware family name in plaintext inside its own pipe-delimited protocol. Decoded beacon payload (repeating heartbeat, sent every ~5 seconds for ~8.5 minutes):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<n> Sec
```

This is STRRAT's documented "ping" check-in format: `ping|STRRAT|<campaign/build ID>|<hostname>|<username>|<OS>|<arch>|<AV product>||<version>|<geo>|<status>|<uptime counter>`. The presence of the literal string "STRRAT" plus the exact field layout is a direct signature match, not a behavioral inference.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — plaintext TCP (no TLS), victim source port 49754. Session ran from 2024-07-30 06:40:05 to 06:48:34 (local capture time), 102 near-identical "ping" beacons observed (7-byte length-prefix frame + ~136–137 byte data frame per cycle), consistent with STRRAT's fixed-interval heartbeat.
- No DNS lookup preceded this connection — the C2 IP is hardcoded/dialed directly, so no associated malicious domain was observed for the C2 channel itself.

**Malware build/campaign ID (from beacon)**
- `1BE8292C`

**Supporting/reconnaissance indicator**
- `GET http://ip-api.com/json/` from 172.16.1.66 — geolocation/IP-reputation self-check immediately preceding sustained C2 activity, a common pre-beacon behavior for this loader family. (Response confirmed victim's public IP/geo: US, Texas, Austin.)

**Transferred files / hashes**
- None observed. No file transfer (HTTP download, SMB write, or otherwise) carrying an executable/jar payload was captured in this pcap, and no SHA256 could be computed from traffic in scope. The capture window (2024-07-30 06:38:48–06:48:34, ~10 minutes) begins after initial infection; only the live STRRAT C2 channel is visible, not the delivery stage.

**Not indicators (benign, ruled out during analysis)**
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209), `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`, `github.com` / `objects.githubusercontent.com` — large but standard-looking TLS sessions, no plaintext STRRAT protocol observed on these; consistent with normal Java/Maven tooling on the host, not confirmed as part of the infection chain.
- `wiresharkworkshop.online` and all its subdomains (DC, LDAP, GPO/SYSVOL/Kerberos traffic) — this is the host's own legitimate Active Directory domain, not attacker infrastructure.
- All Microsoft/MSN/Bing/Office/Skype TLS destinations — routine Windows/Office telemetry and connectivity checks.

## Summary
DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user ccollier, is actively beaconing to a STRRAT command-and-control server at 141.98.10.79:12132 over plaintext TCP. Attribution is signature-confirmed from the malware's own "STRRAT" string embedded in its check-in protocol. Recommend isolating the host immediately, capturing memory/disk for the STRRAT jar and its persistence mechanism, resetting ccollier's domain credentials, and blocking 141.98.10.79 at the perimeter.
